q: What is the difference between water withdrawal and water consumption in BRSR?
title: Water withdrawal vs consumption
short: Withdrawal is all the water you take in from every source. Consumption is the part that does not leave as discharge: withdrawal minus discharge, adjusted if stored water changes a lot. A plant that takes 10,000 kL and discharges 6,500 kL consumes 3,500 kL.
audience: Plant and EHS teams filling water fields

ul: Withdrawal: municipal or industrial supply bills, borewell meter readings, tanker invoices in kL, and harvested rainwater if metered.
Discharge: effluent meter readings, CETP invoices, and ETP outlet logs.
Consumption: the difference, usually water lost in evaporation, product and cooling towers.
Reporting bills in rupees instead of kL.
Counting recycled ETP water as new withdrawal; it is reuse, not a new source.
Leaving out tanker water because it arrives without a meter. The invoice quantity is the record.

p: Withdrawal shows pressure on local sources. Consumption shows how much water the site removes from the area for good, which is what water-stressed regions care about.

example.title: Worked example
lines: Municipal supply 6,000 kL + borewell 3,000 kL + tanker 1,000 kL = withdrawal 10,000 kL.

senseible: Senseible reads kWh, litres and kg from electricity bills and fuel invoices into a dated record per site, with the factor and source on every line, and prepares BRSR drafts from that data. Reports are self-declared drafts.
